# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Jamois_2019_obinutuzumab"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Jamois_2019_obinutuzumab"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1111/bcp.13920> (open access; the final
  parameter estimates are in Supporting Information Tables S1 and S2)

Obinutuzumab is a glycoengineered type II anti-CD20 IgG1 monoclonal antibody.
Jamois 2019 updated the obinutuzumab population PK model of Gibiansky 2014
(available in this package as `Gibiansky_2014_obinutuzumab`) with the data of
the phase III GALLIUM trial in previously untreated follicular lymphoma (FL),
and used it to derive each patient's average concentration over induction
(`CmeanIND`) for an exposure-response analysis of progression-free survival.
The model is two-compartment. Total clearance is a time-independent component
`CL_inf` plus a time-dependent component `CL_T` that decays exponentially with
time since the first dose, as CD20+ target cells are eliminated:

`CL(t) = CL_inf + CL_T * exp(-k_des * t)`

The decay rate `k_des` depends on the chemotherapy given with obinutuzumab
(CHOP or CVP, bendamustine, fludarabine + cyclophosphamide).

The paper's exposure-response analysis of progression-free survival is a
semi-parametric Cox proportional-hazards model. Its baseline hazard is not
estimated and its hazard ratios are shown only graphically (Figure 5), so it
cannot be simulated and the library model covers the PK only.

# Population

The PK dataset combined the dataset of Gibiansky 2014 (678 patients with
chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL), follicular and other indolent non-Hodgkin
lymphoma, diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) or mantle cell lymphoma (MCL)
from the GAUGUIN, GAUDI, GAUSS and CLL11 studies) with 408 GALLIUM patients
(Results, "PK analysis"); the pooled total is not stated. In GALLIUM,
obinutuzumab 1000 mg was infused on days 1, 8 and 15 of cycle 1 and on day 1
of later cycles, with bendamustine (6 x 28-day cycles, 8000 mg in total) or
with CHOP or CVP (8 x 21-day cycles, 10,000 mg in total), followed in
responders by 1000 mg every 2 months for up to 2 years.

The 401 GALLIUM patients of the exposure analysis (Table S3) had a median age
of 59 (27-88) years, median weight 73.7 (35.3-155) kg, 47.4% were male, the
median baseline tumour burden (sum of the products of the perpendicular
diameters of the target lesions) was 5109 (235-80,720) mm^2, and 212 received
bendamustine, 130 CHOP and 59 CVP.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Jamois_2019_obinutuzumab")()$population`.

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment pointing to its source. Values
come from Table S1. The reference covariate values (75 kg, female, 65 years,
albumin 40 g/L, tumour size 3000 mm^2, FL, no chemotherapy, no anti-drug
antibodies) and the assignment of each effect to `CL_T` or `CL_inf` come from
Table S2.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| `lcl_exp_kdes` (k_des) | log(0.112 1/day) | Table S1, theta1 |
| `lcl_exp_component` (CL_T) | log(0.145 L/day) | Table S1, theta2 |
| `lcl_exp_inf` (CL_inf) | log(0.0753 L/day) | Table S1, theta3 |
| `lvc` (V1) | log(2.59 L) | Table S1, theta4 |
| `lvp` (V2) | log(1.47 L) | Table S1, theta5 |
| `lq` (Q) | log(1.32 L/day) | Table S1, theta6 |
| `e_wt_cl_exp_inf`, `e_wt_vc`, `e_wt_vp` | 0.721, 0.437, 0.776 | Table S1, theta7-theta9; `(WT/75)^theta` (Table S2) |
| `e_conmed_chop_cl_exp_kdes` | log(0.285) | Table S1, theta10 (CHOP or CVP) |
| `e_conmed_bendamustine_cl_exp_kdes` | log(0.466) | Table S1, theta11 |
| `e_conmed_fc_cl_exp_kdes` | log(2.88) | Table S1, theta12 |
| `e_mzl_cl_exp_component`, `e_cll_cl_exp_component`, `e_mcl_cl_exp_component` | log(1.4), log(2.28), log(2.98) | Table S1, theta13-theta15 |
| `e_tumsz_cl_exp_component` | 0.345 | Table S1, theta16; `(BSIZ/3000)^theta` (Table S2) |
| `e_sex_cl_exp_component` | log(1.48) | Table S1, theta17 (male vs female) |
| `e_sll_cl_exp_inf`, `e_cll_cl_exp_inf`, `e_mcl_cl_exp_inf` | log(1.38), log(1.45), log(2.04) | Table S1, theta18-theta20; on CL_inf per Table S2 |
| `e_tumsz_cl_exp_inf` | 0.0596 | Table S1, theta21; `(BSIZ/3000)^theta` |
| `e_sex_cl_exp_inf` | log(1.18) | Table S1, theta22 |
| `e_age_cl_exp_inf` | -0.211 | Table S1, theta23; `(AGE/65)^theta` |
| `e_alb_cl_exp_inf` | -0.493 | Table S1, theta24; `(ALB/40)^theta` |
| `e_sex_vc` | log(1.19) | Table S1, theta25 |
| `sdL`, `sdH`, `sd50` | 1.59, 0.121, 7.55 ug/mL | Table S1, theta26-theta28 |
| `e_ada_cl_exp_component`, `e_ada_cl_exp_kdes` | log(3.09), log(1.74) | Table S1, theta29-theta30 |
| `etalcl_exp_kdes`, `etalcl_exp_component`, `etalcl_exp_inf` | 0.821, 1.09, 0.163 | Table S1, Omega(1,1)-Omega(3,3) |
| `etalvc`, `etalvp`, `etalq` | 0.0355, 0.143, 0.997 | Table S1, Omega(4,4)-Omega(6,6) |
| `etaRUV` | 0.191 | Table S1, Omega(7,7) 'EPS', IIV on the residual SD |
| `cl <- cl_exp_component * exp(-cl_exp_kdes * time) + cl_exp_inf` | n/a | Results and Discussion (time-dependent and time-independent clearance); Gibiansky 2014 structure |
| `d/dt(central)`, `d/dt(peripheral1)` | n/a | Two-compartment model of Gibiansky 2014, which this model updates |
| `w <- (sdL - (sdL - sdH) * Cc / (sd50 + Cc)) * exp(etaRUV)`; `Cc ~ lnorm(w)` | n/a | Not printed in Jamois 2019; see Assumptions and deviations |

# Deterministic checks of the model file

## Covariate effects (Table S2)

Table S2 lists the percentage change of each parameter at low and high
covariate values relative to the reference subject. These follow from the
typical values and the functional forms alone, so the packaged model must
reproduce them to the rounding of Table S1.

```{r tableS2}
mod <- readModelDb("Jamois_2019_obinutuzumab")

ref <- data.frame(
  WT = 75, SEXF = 1, TUMSZ = 3000, ALB = 40, AGE = 65,
  TUMTP_CLL = 0, TUMTP_SLL = 0, TUMTP_MCL = 0, TUMTP_MZL = 0,
  CONMED_CHOP = 0, CONMED_BENDAMUSTINE = 0, CONMED_FC = 0, ADA_POS = 0
)
scen <- tibble::tribble(
  ~parameter, ~covariate, ~value, ~published,
  "cl_exp_inf", "WT", 50, -25.3,
  "cl_exp_inf", "WT", 115, 36.1,
  "cl_exp_inf", "ALB", 29.0, 17.2,
  "cl_exp_inf", "ALB", 48.6, -9.2,
  "cl_exp_inf", "SEXF", 0, 17.7,
  "cl_exp_inf", "TUMTP_CLL", 1, 45.2,
  "cl_exp_inf", "TUMTP_SLL", 1, 38.0,
  "cl_exp_inf", "TUMTP_MCL", 1, 104.3,
  "cl_exp_inf", "AGE", 38, 12.0,
  "cl_exp_inf", "AGE", 82, -4.8,
  "cl_exp_inf", "TUMSZ", 344, -12.1,
  "cl_exp_inf", "TUMSZ", 27500, 14.1,
  "cl_exp_component", "SEXF", 0, 48.3,
  "cl_exp_component", "TUMTP_CLL", 1, 128.3,
  "cl_exp_component", "TUMTP_MCL", 1, 197.8,
  "cl_exp_component", "TUMTP_MZL", 1, 40.2,
  "cl_exp_component", "TUMSZ", 344, -52.7,
  "cl_exp_component", "TUMSZ", 27500, 115,
  "cl_exp_component", "ADA_POS", 1, 209.2,
  "vc", "WT", 50, -16.2,
  "vc", "WT", 115, 20.6,
  "vc", "SEXF", 0, 18.6,
  "vp", "WT", 50, -27.0,
  "vp", "WT", 115, 39.3,
  "cl_exp_kdes", "CONMED_CHOP", 1, -71.5,
  "cl_exp_kdes", "CONMED_FC", 1, 187.6,
  "cl_exp_kdes", "CONMED_BENDAMUSTINE", 1, -53.4,
  "cl_exp_kdes", "ADA_POS", 1, 74.4
)

# One subject per scenario (id 1 is the reference subject); a single
# observation at time 0 returns the individual parameters.
cov_rows <- ref[rep(1, nrow(scen) + 1), ]
for (i in seq_len(nrow(scen))) {
  cov_rows[i + 1, scen$covariate[i]] <- scen$value[i]
}
ev_par <- cbind(id = seq_len(nrow(cov_rows)), time = 0, evid = 0, cmt = "central", cov_rows)
par <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_par, omega = NA, returnType = "data.frame")
stopifnot(nrow(par) == nrow(scen) + 1)

scen$model <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(scen)), function(i) {
  100 * (par[[scen$parameter[i]]][i + 1] / par[[scen$parameter[i]]][1] - 1)
}, numeric(1))

scen |>
  dplyr::mutate(model = round(model, 1)) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Parameter" = parameter, "Covariate" = covariate, "Covariate value" = value,
    "Published change (%)" = published, "Model change (%)" = model
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Covariate effects: model versus Table S2 of Jamois 2019.")

# Table S2 was computed from unrounded estimates; Table S1 prints three
# significant figures, so ratios agree to about 0.4% (e.g. 1.19 vs 1.186 for
# sex on V1). A wrong reference value or functional form moves a row by
# several percentage points.
ratio_err <- abs((1 + scen$model / 100) / (1 + scen$published / 100) - 1)
stopifnot(max(ratio_err) < 0.005)
```

## Decay of the time-dependent clearance

The Results give the half-life of the decay of `CL_T` as 13.2 days with
bendamustine and 21.6 days with CHOP or CVP.

```{r kdes-half-life}
thalf <- c(
  bendamustine = log(2) / par$cl_exp_kdes[which(scen$covariate == "CONMED_BENDAMUSTINE") + 1],
  chop_cvp = log(2) / par$cl_exp_kdes[which(scen$covariate == "CONMED_CHOP") + 1]
)
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Backbone = c("Bendamustine", "CHOP or CVP"),
  Published = c(13.2, 21.6),
  Model = round(unname(thalf), 2)
), caption = "Half-life (days) of the decay of the time-dependent clearance.")

# 0.112 * 0.466 and 0.112 * 0.285 from the rounded Table S1 values give
# 13.28 and 21.72 days.
stopifnot(
  abs(thalf[["bendamustine"]] / 13.2 - 1) < 0.01,
  abs(thalf[["chop_cvp"]] / 21.6 - 1) < 0.01
)
```

## Residual error

The residual SD on the log scale falls from `sdL` = 1.59 at low
concentrations to `sdH` = 0.121 at high concentrations, and is halfway
between them at `sd50` = 7.55 ug/mL.

```{r residual}
theta <- rxode2::rxode(mod)$theta
w_at <- function(conc) {
  theta[["sdL"]] - (theta[["sdL"]] - theta[["sdH"]]) * conc / (theta[["sd50"]] + conc)
}
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  `Concentration (ug/mL)` = c(0.00405, 7.55, 100, 500),
  `Residual SD (log scale)` = round(w_at(c(0.00405, 7.55, 100, 500)), 3),
  check.names = FALSE
), caption = "Typical residual SD at the LLOQ (4.05 ng/mL), at sd50 and in the therapeutic range.")
stopifnot(abs(w_at(7.55) - (1.59 + 0.121) / 2) < 1e-9)
```

# Typical concentration-time profiles (Figure 2)

Figure 2 shows typical profiles over a 3-weekly induction (8 cycles) followed
by maintenance every 8 weeks. The paper does not state the covariates held
fixed in each panel; here the other covariates are the reference values
(female, 75 kg, 65 years, albumin 40 g/L, 3000 mm^2), with CHOP or CVP.

```{r figure2, fig.height = 7}
dose_chop <- c(0, 7, 14, 21 * (1:7))
dose_maint <- 147 + 56 * (1:4)
dose_fig2 <- c(dose_chop, dose_maint)
grid_fig2 <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 600, by = 0.5), dose_fig2 + 4 / 24)))

make_events <- function(dose_times, obs_times, n_id = 1) {
  ev <- rxode2::et(amt = 1000, time = dose_times, dur = 4 / 24, cmt = "central") |>
    rxode2::et(obs_times, cmt = "central")
  ev <- as.data.frame(ev)
  ev <- ev[, setdiff(names(ev), "id")]
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(n_id), function(i) cbind(id = i, ev)))
}

panels <- tibble::tribble(
  ~panel, ~label, ~covariate, ~value,
  "A: body weight", "50 kg", "WT", 50,
  "A: body weight", "75 kg", "WT", 75,
  "A: body weight", "115 kg", "WT", 115,
  "B: sex", "Female", "SEXF", 1,
  "B: sex", "Male", "SEXF", 0,
  "C: tumour size", "600 mm^2", "TUMSZ", 600,
  "C: tumour size", "4000 mm^2", "TUMSZ", 4000,
  "C: tumour size", "16000 mm^2", "TUMSZ", 16000
)
ref_chop <- ref
ref_chop$CONMED_CHOP <- 1
ev_fig2 <- make_events(dose_fig2, grid_fig2, n_id = nrow(panels))
cov_fig2 <- ref_chop[rep(1, nrow(panels)), ]
for (i in seq_len(nrow(panels))) cov_fig2[i, panels$covariate[i]] <- panels$value[i]
cov_fig2$id <- seq_len(nrow(panels))
ev_fig2 <- dplyr::left_join(ev_fig2, cov_fig2, by = "id")

sim_fig2 <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_fig2, omega = NA, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::mutate(panels, id = dplyr::row_number()), by = "id")

ggplot(sim_fig2, aes(time / 7, Cc, colour = label)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 1) +
  labs(x = "Time (week)", y = "Obinutuzumab concentration (ug/mL)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw()

# Peak after the last induction infusion (day 147), per scenario.
peak21 <- sim_fig2 |>
  dplyr::filter(abs(time - (147 + 4 / 24)) < 1e-6) |>
  dplyr::select(panel, label, Cc)
knitr::kable(
  dplyr::rename(peak21, "Panel" = panel, "Scenario" = label, "Peak at week 21 (ug/mL)" = Cc) |>
    dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(3, round)),
  caption = "Typical peak concentration after the last induction infusion."
)
pk <- setNames(peak21$Cc, peak21$label)
stopifnot(
  nrow(peak21) == nrow(panels),
  pk[["50 kg"]] > pk[["75 kg"]], pk[["75 kg"]] > pk[["115 kg"]],
  pk[["Female"]] > pk[["Male"]],
  pk[["600 mm^2"]] > pk[["4000 mm^2"]], pk[["4000 mm^2"]] > pk[["16000 mm^2"]]
)
```

Replicates Figure 2 of Jamois 2019. The model reproduces the ordering of the
published panels (lower exposure with higher body weight, in males and with
larger tumours). Its typical peaks after the last induction infusion are
`r round(min(pk))`-`r round(max(pk))` ug/mL, about 5-15% above the values
read by eye from the published panels (about 560-900 ug/mL). The covariates
held fixed in each published panel are not stated (the reference values are
used here), so the curves are not compared point by point.

# Exposure during induction in GALLIUM (Table 1)

## Virtual cohort

Table 1 summarises individual `AUCtau` over the last induction cycle and
`CmeanIND` (cumulative AUC over the induction period divided by its duration)
in the 401 FL patients of the exposure analysis. The induction period ends one
cycle after the last induction dose: day 168 in both arms (cycle 6 dose on day
140 + 28 days with bendamustine; cycle 8 dose on day 147 + 21 days with CHOP or
CVP). Here 200 virtual patients per arm are drawn from the Table S3
demographics.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20190312)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20190312)

n_per_arm <- 200

draw_truncated <- function(n, draw, lower, upper) {
  out <- numeric(0)
  while (length(out) < n) {
    x <- draw(n)
    out <- c(out, x[x >= lower & x <= upper])
  }
  out[seq_len(n)]
}

make_cohort <- function(n, arm) {
  data.frame(
    WT = draw_truncated(n, function(k) rlnorm(k, log(73.7), 0.2), 35.3, 155),
    SEXF = rbinom(n, 1, 1 - 0.474),
    AGE = draw_truncated(n, function(k) rnorm(k, 59, 11), 27, 88),
    TUMSZ = draw_truncated(n, function(k) rlnorm(k, log(5109), 1.0), 235, 80720),
    ALB = draw_truncated(n, function(k) rnorm(k, 40, 5), 25, 55),
    TUMTP_CLL = 0, TUMTP_SLL = 0, TUMTP_MCL = 0, TUMTP_MZL = 0,
    CONMED_CHOP = as.integer(arm == "G-CHOP/CVP"),
    CONMED_BENDAMUSTINE = as.integer(arm == "G-Benda"),
    CONMED_FC = 0, ADA_POS = 0,
    treatment = arm
  )
}
cohort <- rbind(make_cohort(n_per_arm, "G-Benda"), make_cohort(n_per_arm, "G-CHOP/CVP"))
cohort$id <- seq_len(nrow(cohort))

dose_benda <- c(0, 7, 14, 28 * (1:5))
obs_grid <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 168, by = 0.1), dose_benda + 4 / 24, dose_chop + 4 / 24)))

ev_benda <- make_events(dose_benda, obs_grid, n_id = n_per_arm)
ev_chop <- make_events(dose_chop, obs_grid, n_id = n_per_arm)
ev_chop$id <- ev_chop$id + n_per_arm
ev_cohort <- dplyr::left_join(rbind(ev_benda, ev_chop), cohort, by = "id")

sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_cohort, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(cohort, id, treatment), by = "id")
```

## NCA with PKNCA

```{r pknca}
conc_df <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
# Time-zero rows are on the observation grid; keep one per subject.
conc_df <- conc_df |>
  dplyr::bind_rows(dplyr::distinct(conc_df, id, treatment) |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time)

dose_df <- ev_cohort |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(amt) & amt > 0) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, treatment)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_df, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id)

intervals <- data.frame(
  treatment = c("G-Benda", "G-Benda", "G-CHOP/CVP", "G-CHOP/CVP"),
  start = c(0, 140, 0, 147),
  end = 168,
  auclast = TRUE
)
nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

exposure <- as.data.frame(nca$result) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  dplyr::mutate(metric = ifelse(start == 0, "cmean_ind", "auc_tau")) |>
  dplyr::select(id, treatment, metric, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = metric, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  dplyr::mutate(cmean_ind = cmean_ind / 168) |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(cohort, id, WT, SEXF, TUMSZ), by = "id")
```

## Comparison with Table 1

```{r table1}
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment, ~subgroup, ~auc_tau, ~cmean_ind,
  "G-Benda", "WT <= 90 kg", 11300, 358,
  "G-Benda", "WT > 90 kg", 7430, 253,
  "G-CHOP/CVP", "WT <= 90 kg", 11600, 454,
  "G-CHOP/CVP", "WT > 90 kg", 7460, 292,
  "G-Benda", "Female", 11900, 382,
  "G-Benda", "Male", 9060, 290,
  "G-CHOP/CVP", "Female", 13000, 487,
  "G-CHOP/CVP", "Male", 9070, 358,
  "G-Benda", "Tumour <= 5109 mm^2", 10800, 339,
  "G-Benda", "Tumour > 5109 mm^2", 10100, 327,
  "G-CHOP/CVP", "Tumour <= 5109 mm^2", 10800, 423,
  "G-CHOP/CVP", "Tumour > 5109 mm^2", 10800, 429
)

subgrouped <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  exposure |> dplyr::mutate(subgroup = ifelse(WT <= 90, "WT <= 90 kg", "WT > 90 kg")),
  exposure |> dplyr::mutate(subgroup = ifelse(SEXF == 1, "Female", "Male")),
  exposure |> dplyr::mutate(subgroup = ifelse(TUMSZ <= 5109, "Tumour <= 5109 mm^2", "Tumour > 5109 mm^2"))
)
simulated <- subgrouped |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, subgroup) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    n = dplyr::n(),
    auc_tau_sim = median(auc_tau),
    cmean_ind_sim = median(cmean_ind),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

cmp <- dplyr::left_join(published, simulated, by = c("treatment", "subgroup")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    auc_pct = 100 * (auc_tau_sim / auc_tau - 1),
    cmean_pct = 100 * (cmean_ind_sim / cmean_ind - 1)
  )

cmp |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    treatment, subgroup, n,
    auc_tau, auc_tau_sim = signif(auc_tau_sim, 3), auc_pct = round(auc_pct, 1),
    cmean_ind, cmean_ind_sim = signif(cmean_ind_sim, 3), cmean_pct = round(cmean_pct, 1)
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Arm" = treatment, "Subgroup" = subgroup, "N simulated" = n,
    "AUCtau published" = auc_tau, "AUCtau simulated" = auc_tau_sim, "AUCtau diff (%)" = auc_pct,
    "CmeanIND published" = cmean_ind, "CmeanIND simulated" = cmean_ind_sim,
    "CmeanIND diff (%)" = cmean_pct
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Median AUCtau (ug/mL day) and CmeanIND (ug/mL): simulation versus Table 1 of Jamois 2019.")
```

```{r table1-check}
pct <- c(cmp$auc_pct, cmp$cmean_pct)
stopifnot(
  # Centre: a wrong clearance, volume or dose unit moves every cell by tens
  # of percent.
  abs(median(pct)) < 10,
  # Envelope over the 24 cells, robust to which subjects land in the tails.
  quantile(abs(pct), 0.9) < 25
)

# Weight and sex trends of Table 1: median CmeanIND above 90 kg and in men is
# lower than at or below 90 kg and in women, in both arms (published ratios
# 0.64-0.76).
med_ratio <- function(arm, hi, lo) {
  cmp$cmean_ind_sim[cmp$treatment == arm & cmp$subgroup == hi] /
    cmp$cmean_ind_sim[cmp$treatment == arm & cmp$subgroup == lo]
}
trend <- c(
  benda_wt = med_ratio("G-Benda", "WT > 90 kg", "WT <= 90 kg"),
  chop_wt = med_ratio("G-CHOP/CVP", "WT > 90 kg", "WT <= 90 kg"),
  benda_sex = med_ratio("G-Benda", "Male", "Female"),
  chop_sex = med_ratio("G-CHOP/CVP", "Male", "Female")
)
stopifnot(all(trend < 1))
```

The simulated medians agree with Table 1 (median difference
`r sprintf("%.1f", median(pct))`% over the 24 cells, largest
`r sprintf("%.0f", max(abs(pct)))`%). The weight and sex trends are reproduced:
median `CmeanIND` is lower above 90 kg and in men in both arms (simulated
ratios `r sprintf("%.2f", min(trend))`-`r sprintf("%.2f", max(trend))`,
published 0.64-0.76).

The tumour-burden split differs more in the simulation than in Table 1, where
exposure is almost the same above and below the median (at most 7% apart).
The virtual cohort draws tumour size independently of the other covariates,
while in GALLIUM tumour burden may be correlated with them; the published
values are also medians of individual post hoc predictions under the actual
dosing history, including delays and dose modifications, whereas the
simulation gives every planned dose on schedule.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Residual-error equation.** Jamois 2019 lists `sigma_L`, `sigma_H` and
  `sigma_50` with `sigma^2` fixed to 1 and an IIV term on the residual error
  (Table S1) but does not print the equation. The same authors define this
  residual model in Gibiansky 2021 (rituximab, CPT Pharmacometrics Syst
  Pharmacol 10:914) and in the supplement of Jamois 2021 (rituximab, Clin
  Pharmacol Ther): an exponential error on log-transformed concentrations
  whose SD is an Emax function of the concentration,
  `W = sigma_L - (sigma_L - sigma_H) * C / (sigma_50 + C)`, so that `W` is
  halfway between `sigma_L` and `sigma_H` at `sigma_50`. That form is used
  here, with the residual IIV multiplying `W` as in
  `Gibiansky_2021_rituximab`.
* **Structural equations.** The paper describes the model as an update of
  Gibiansky 2014 with time-dependent and time-independent clearances and does
  not reprint the equations; the two-compartment structure and
  `CL(t) = CL_inf + CL_T * exp(-k_des * t)` are those of Gibiansky 2014.
* **Covariate forms.** Continuous covariates use power models normalised to
  the Table S2 reference values and categorical covariates multiply the
  parameter by `exp(theta)`. Both are confirmed by the reproduction of every
  row of Table S2 above.
* **Assignment of effects.** Table S2 places the CLL, SLL, MCL, sex, tumour
  size, age and albumin effects of theta18-theta24 on `CL_inf`; the Table S1
  footnote calls the SLL effect an effect "on CL (total clearance)". The model
  follows Table S2: its `CL_T` rows (for example CLL +128.3%) equal the
  `CL_T` thetas alone, which would not hold if theta19 also multiplied `CL_T`.
* **No body-weight effect on CL_T or Q.** Table S1 lists weight exponents only
  for `CL_inf`, V1 and V2, and Table S2 lists no weight effect on `CL_T` or Q.
  Gibiansky 2014 had a fixed allometric exponent on Q; none is applied here.
* **Disease reference.** The reference histology is FL (pooled with DLBCL,
  and with MZL for `CL_inf`). The library model has no separate DLBCL
  indicator because the paper reports no DLBCL effect.
* **Time-dependent clearance clock.** `time` is the time since the first
  obinutuzumab dose. The model does not reset the decay for later treatment
  courses.
* **Virtual cohort.** Weight, age and tumour size distributions are
  log-normal or normal fits to the Table S3 medians and ranges; albumin is
  not reported for GALLIUM and is drawn around the 40 g/L reference (SD 5 g/L,
  consistent with the 29.0-48.6 g/L 2.5th-97.5th percentiles in Table S2).
  All virtual patients are anti-drug antibody negative. The infusion duration
  is not given in the paper; 4 hours is used for every infusion, which has no
  material effect on AUC over days.
* **Statements not reproduced.** The Results state that "the initial total
  clearance ... is 4.4-fold higher than the nonspecific time-independent
  clearance". For the reference subject `(CL_T + CL_inf) / CL_inf` is
  `r sprintf("%.2f", (par$cl_exp_component[1] + par$cl_exp_inf[1]) / par$cl_exp_inf[1])`,
  and the paper does not say for which subject or summary the 4.4 was
  computed, so it is not used as a check.
* **Exposure-response model.** The Cox proportional-hazards model of
  progression-free survival (Figure 5) has no estimated baseline hazard and
  its coefficients are shown only as a forest plot, so it is not part of the
  library model.
